A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PAWS-VMK research despite the changed title and organization. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original semi-supervised classification and OOD detection results, component ablations, prototype-selection analyses, and transfer experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a CIFAR-10 experiment incorporating PALM's prototype-contrastive loss.

M1.justification: The three-component pipeline is retained, but the stated vMF-SNE concentration-selection rule changes its entropy target from gamma to log gamma (v2 Section 3.2; v3 Appendix A). This revises the described calibration rule; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven classification datasets, binary DeepWeeds task, and CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 near- and far-OOD suites. The added PALM-loss experiment uses the existing CIFAR-10 classification task.

E2.justification: v3 Table S10 adds PAWS and PAWS-M variants incorporating PALM's prototype-contrastive term as comparison conditions. The existing SSL and OOD baseline sets remain unchanged; this is not a newly added evaluation of the full PALM method.

E3.justification: Table S10 introduces a controlled CIFAR-10 comparison crossing consistency versus PAWS-MixMatch loss with the PALM term enabled versus disabled. The retained experiments preserve their splits, label budgets, backbone configurations, and 50-epoch training and 20-epoch initialization budgets.

E4.justification: The new PALM-loss ablation tests whether explicitly encouraging prototype compactness improves SSL, finding reduced accuracy in both tested loss settings. Existing component, hyperparameter, transfer, RoPAWS, and prototype-diversity analyses are retained, often relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting, 20-run prototype-coverage analyses with minimum/maximum error bars, and predominantly single-run alternative-hyperparameter tests. Table S10 adds uncertainty values without introducing a different reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table S10 reports CIFAR-10 accuracy with versus without the PALM term: 92.1±0.1 versus 92.9±0.2 for PAWS, and 94.2±0.1 versus 95.9±0.1 for PAWS-M. The corresponding pre-existing benchmark tables and plotted results are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A revises the entropy/perplexity equation from sum p log p = gamma to sum p log p = log gamma. v3 also supplies the PALM loss expression in Equation 17. The existing PAWS probabilistic derivation is relocated, rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract softens SKMPS's claimed superiority over other selection approaches to competitive performance. The principal three-component contribution and headline SSL/OOD performance claims remain, while the new conclusion largely restates them.

C2.justification: v3 adds the argument that combining PAWS and PALM is nontrivial because a loss encouraging compact OOD representations can conflict with SSL accuracy. This qualifies the earlier discussion of compactness benefits using the new Table S10 experiment.

D1.justification: New Algorithms 1 and 2 document vMF-SNE initialization and SKMPS, including initial concentration values and the sequence of minibatch calculations. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware and timing information, and implementation-access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hinton and colleagues' knowledge-distillation work and an embedding-initialization analogy, removes four general prototype-learning/self-supervised references, and expands the comparison between PAWS and PALM. Most related-work coverage remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Mathematical details and SSL ablations move into reorganized appendices, a conclusion is added, and terminology changes throughout from pretraining to initialization and from MixMatch to PAWS-MixMatch.

P2.justification: The document adopts different typography, margins, and extensive figure/table resizing and relocation. v2 Figures 2 and 3 become supplementary Figures S6 and S5; v3 adds Table S10 and two algorithm displays. Figure S8(b) also corrects the axis label from 'Proportion of classes' to 'Proportion complete' without changing its bars.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens the design rationale through the PALM-loss ablation, clarifies the joint SSL/OOD motivation, and corrects the misleading prototype-coverage axis label. The reorganized exposition is useful, although the new pseudocode contains normalization and entropy-sign ambiguities. These are limited gains rather than a substantial strengthening of the unchanged benchmark evidence.
